args.body:
ACCOUNT CONTROL AGREEMENT
TRACKED-CHANGES REDLINE
(Counterparty Draft → Lender/Secured Party Required Form)

Matter: Review Account Control Agreement — Counterparty Paper
Document: aca-redline.docx
Status: Counsel markup for circulation to counterparty and depository bank
Base: Counterparty draft ACA, reconciled to (i) internal ACA Playbook, (ii) Executed Credit Agreement (as defined), (iii) Depository Bank standard form, (iv) Account Details Schedule, (v) Exhibit B Survival Matrix, (vi) Schedules 3.7 and 5.2, and (vii) controlling deal-team instruction (latest partner email)
Legend: [DELETE: text] = deletion required | [INSERT: text] = insertion required | [MOVE] / comments in braces {Comment: …}

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
ACCOUNT CONTROL AGREEMENT
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

This ACCOUNT CONTROL AGREEMENT (this "Agreement"), dated as of [●], 20[●] (the "Effective Date"), is entered into by and among:

(1) [BORROWER / GRANTOR LEGAL NAME], a [jurisdiction] [entity type] (the "Grantor");
(2) [ADMINISTRATIVE AGENT LEGAL NAME], as administrative agent and collateral agent for the Secured Parties (in such capacity, together with its successors and assigns, the "Secured Party"); and
(3) [DEPOSITORY BANK LEGAL NAME] (the "Bank").

RECITALS

A. The Grantor, the lenders party thereto from time to time, and the Secured Party have entered into that certain [Credit Agreement], dated as of [●] (as amended, restated, supplemented, or otherwise modified from time to time, the "Credit Agreement").

B. Pursuant to the Credit Agreement and the other Loan Documents, the Grantor has granted to the Secured Party a security interest in, among other things, the Deposit Accounts (as defined below).

C. The parties are entering into this Agreement to perfect the Secured Party's security interest in the Deposit Accounts by "control" under Article 9 of the Uniform Commercial Code and to set forth the Bank's agreements with respect thereto.

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants herein and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the parties agree as follows:

───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ARTICLE I — DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATION
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Section 1.1 Definitions. Capitalized terms used but not defined herein have the meanings assigned in the Credit Agreement. As used herein:

"Account Details Schedule" means Schedule I attached hereto, as updated from time to time in accordance with Section 2.4.

"Business Day" means any day other than a Saturday, Sunday, or day on which banks in New York, New York are authorized or required by law to close.

"Control Notice" [INSERT: (also referred to as an "Activation Notice" or "Notice of Exclusive Control")] means a written notice from the Secured Party to the Bank substantially in the form of Exhibit A, stating that the Secured Party is exercising exclusive control over the Deposit Accounts.

"Deposit Accounts" means each deposit account maintained by the Grantor with the Bank and identified on the Account Details Schedule, together with all cash, funds, financial assets, and other property credited thereto or carried therein, all interest and proceeds thereof, and all renewals, replacements, and substitutions therefor, whether now existing or hereafter established.

[INSERT: "Excluded Claims" means claims arising from (a) the Bank's gross negligence, willful misconduct, or bad faith, as determined by a final non-appealable judgment of a court of competent jurisdiction, (b) the Bank's breach of this Agreement, or (c) the Bank's failure to comply with entitlement orders or instructions originated by the Secured Party after delivery of a Control Notice in accordance with this Agreement.]

[INSERT: "Indemnified Liabilities" has the meaning set forth in Section 7.1.]

"Loan Documents" has the meaning set forth in the Credit Agreement.

[DELETE: "Material Adverse Effect" means a material adverse effect on (a) the business, assets, properties, liabilities, financial condition, or results of operations of the Grantor, (b) the ability of the Grantor to perform its obligations under this Agreement, (c) the validity or enforceability of this Agreement, or (d) the rights and remedies of the Secured Party or the Bank hereunder; provided, however, that none of the following shall constitute, or be taken into account in determining whether there has been, a Material Adverse Effect: (i) any regulatory action, inquiry, investigation, examination, or proceeding by any Governmental Authority; (ii) any change in Applicable Law or regulatory policy; or (iii) any matter disclosed on any schedule to any Loan Document.]

[INSERT: "Material Adverse Effect" means a material adverse effect on (a) the business, assets, properties, liabilities (actual or contingent), financial condition, or results of operations of the Grantor and its Subsidiaries, taken as a whole, (b) the ability of the Grantor to perform its payment or other material obligations under this Agreement or any other Loan Document, (c) the validity, enforceability, perfection, or priority of this Agreement or the Liens granted under the Loan Documents, or (d) the rights and remedies of the Secured Party under this Agreement or any other Loan Document. For the avoidance of doubt, and notwithstanding any disclosure on Schedule 3.7 or otherwise, no carve-out shall exclude from "Material Adverse Effect" any regulatory action, inquiry, investigation, examination, enforcement proceeding, or Order that (x) relates to the Deposit Accounts, the Collateral, the Loan Documents, or the transactions contemplated thereby, (y) challenges the validity, perfection, or priority of the Secured Party's Lien, or (z) could reasonably be expected to impair the Secured Party's control over, or access to, the Deposit Accounts or the proceeds thereof.]

{Comment — §1.1 MAE: Counterparty draft silently added broad regulatory-action carve-outs. Playbook §4.2 and Credit Agreement §1.01 require lender-protective MAE with no regulatory carve-out that would nullify pending inquiries disclosed on Schedule 3.7. Restore Credit Agreement-aligned definition; expressly override Schedule 3.7 as a MAE safe harbor.}

"Obligations" has the meaning set forth in the Credit Agreement.

"Secured Parties" has the meaning set forth in the Credit Agreement.

"UCC" means the Uniform Commercial Code as in effect from time to time in the State of New York (or, where applicable to perfection or priority, the UCC of another jurisdiction).

Section 1.2 UCC Terms. "Control," "deposit account," "entitlement order," "financial asset," "proceeds," and other UCC terms used herein have the meanings assigned in Articles 8 and 9 of the UCC.

Section 1.3 Rules of Construction. The rules of construction set forth in the Credit Agreement apply mutatis mutandis. [INSERT: In the event of any conflict between this Agreement and the Credit Agreement with respect to the Secured Party's rights in the Collateral, the Credit Agreement shall control as between the Grantor and the Secured Party; provided that, as among the Bank, the Grantor, and the Secured Party, this Agreement shall control with respect to the Bank's duties, the mechanics of control, and the Bank's indemnities and limitations of liability.] References to Schedules and Exhibits are to those attached hereto. [INSERT: The Account Details Schedule, Exhibit A (Form of Control Notice), Exhibit B (Survival Matrix), and any joinder or amendment hereafter executed are incorporated by reference and form part of this Agreement.]

───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ARTICLE II — THE DEPOSIT ACCOUNTS; ESTABLISHMENT OF CONTROL
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Section 2.1 Identification of Deposit Accounts. The Grantor represents and warrants that the Deposit Accounts listed on the Account Details Schedule are all of the deposit accounts maintained by the Grantor with the Bank as of the Effective Date, and that each is a "deposit account" under UCC §9-102. [INSERT: The Grantor shall not maintain any other deposit account with the Bank unless such account is promptly added to the Account Details Schedule by written notice to the Secured Party and the Bank and becomes subject to this Agreement.]

Section 2.2 Agreement to Follow Secured Party Instructions — Control.
(a) The Bank agrees that it will comply with [DELETE: instructions] [INSERT: entitlement orders and other instructions] originated by the Secured Party concerning the Deposit Accounts without further consent by the Grantor [INSERT: or any other Person].
(b) [INSERT: The parties acknowledge and agree that this Agreement is intended to, and does, confer "control" of each Deposit Account on the Secured Party within the meaning of UCC §§9-104(a)(2) and 8-106, and that the Secured Party's security interest in each Deposit Account is perfected by control.]
(c) Until the Bank receives a Control Notice, the Bank may comply with instructions originated by the Grantor concerning the Deposit Accounts, including instructions for withdrawal, transfer, or payment [INSERT: ; provided that the Bank shall not permit any withdrawal, transfer, or disposition that the Bank has been instructed in writing by the Secured Party to prohibit, whether or not a Control Notice has been delivered].
(d) After the Bank receives a Control Notice, the Bank shall (i) cease complying with instructions originated by the Grantor, (ii) comply solely with entitlement orders and instructions originated by the Secured Party, and (iii) [INSERT: not exercise any setoff, recoupment, banker's lien, or similar right against the Deposit Accounts except as expressly permitted under Section 4.2].

{Comment — §2.2: Align with Bank standard form control mechanics and Playbook §2.1 (exclusive control post-notice; pre-notice negative control optional but preferred). Insert express UCC §9-104 acknowledgment required by Credit Agreement §[Collateral] and closing checklist Item C-4.}

Section 2.3 Subordination of Bank Liens; Waiver of Setoff (Pre-Default Mechanics).
(a) The Bank hereby subordinates any security interest, lien, right of setoff, recoupment, or banker's lien it may have in or against the Deposit Accounts [DELETE: to the extent of collected balances available after payment of the Bank's fees] [INSERT: to the security interest and Lien of the Secured Party, except only for the Bank's right to charge the Deposit Accounts for its customary fees and charges for maintaining the Deposit Accounts and for returned items, reversals, and corrections, in each case in the ordinary course and consistent with the Bank's standard fee schedule disclosed to the Secured Party (the "Permitted Bank Charges")].
(b) [INSERT: Except for Permitted Bank Charges, the Bank irrevocably waives and agrees not to assert any setoff, recoupment, counterclaim, or banker's lien against the Deposit Accounts as to amounts owed by the Grantor or any Affiliate to the Bank, whether arising under deposit account agreements, loan facilities, treasury services, or otherwise.]
(c) [INSERT: The subordination and waiver in this Section 2.3 are continuing and irrevocable until the Bank receives written notice from the Secured Party that all Obligations have been Paid in Full and the Credit Agreement collateral release provisions have been satisfied.]

{Comment — §2.3: Counterparty/bank-leaning draft diluted subordination. Playbook §3.1 and Credit Agreement §[Negative Pledge / Cash Management] require broad subordination with only narrow ordinary-course fee carve-out. Restore full waiver of affiliate/setoff exposure.}

Section 2.4 Changes to Deposit Accounts. The Grantor shall not close, rename, or transfer any Deposit Account, or open any additional deposit account with the Bank, without [DELETE: prior notice to] [INSERT: not less than five (5) Business Days' prior written notice to, and as to additional accounts the prior written consent of,] the Secured Party. Any additional account shall automatically become a Deposit Account hereunder upon notice to the Bank and updating of the Account Details Schedule [INSERT: , and the Bank shall execute a short-form acknowledgment or joinder if reasonably requested by the Secured Party].

Section 2.5 Account Details; Statements. The Bank shall provide to the Secured Party, [DELETE: upon request] [INSERT: concurrently with delivery to the Grantor and in any event within five (5) Business Days after month-end, and promptly upon request], copies of account statements, transaction activity, and balance information for the Deposit Accounts [INSERT: in electronic form reasonably acceptable to the Secured Party]. [INSERT: The Grantor hereby authorizes the Bank to provide such information to the Secured Party without further consent.]

Section 2.6 No Other Control Agreements. The Grantor and the Bank represent that, except for this Agreement, there is no agreement under which the Bank is obligated to comply with instructions of any Person other than the Grantor concerning the Deposit Accounts. [INSERT: Neither the Grantor nor the Bank shall enter into any other control agreement, control arrangement, or similar agreement with respect to any Deposit Account without the prior written consent of the Secured Party.]

───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ARTICLE III — REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Section 3.1 Grantor Representations. The Grantor represents and warrants to the Secured Party and the Bank as of the Effective Date [INSERT: and on each date on which a Deposit Account is added] that:
(a) it has full power and authority to execute, deliver, and perform this Agreement;
(b) this Agreement has been duly authorized, executed, and delivered and constitutes its legal, valid, and binding obligation, enforceable in accordance with its terms;
(c) the execution and performance of this Agreement do not conflict with its organizational documents, any material agreement binding upon it, or Applicable Law;
(d) it is the sole account holder of each Deposit Account, and no other Person has any ownership or other interest therein (other than the Secured Party's security interest and the Bank's limited rights expressly preserved herein);
(e) [INSERT: the Deposit Accounts are not subject to any Lien other than Permitted Liens expressly permitted under the Credit Agreement that are junior and subordinated as provided herein;]
(f) [INSERT: except as set forth on Schedule 3.7 (which discloses two pending regulatory inquiries), there is no action, suit, investigation, or proceeding pending or, to the Grantor's knowledge, threatened that could reasonably be expected to affect the Deposit Accounts, the Secured Party's control, or the enforceability of this Agreement; provided that the existence of the matters on Schedule 3.7 does not, and shall not be construed to, qualify, limit, or constitute a carve-out from the definition of Material Adverse Effect or from any indemnity, covenant, or remedy under this Agreement or the Credit Agreement;] and
(g) all information provided to the Secured Party regarding the Deposit Accounts is true, correct, and complete in all material respects.

{Comment — §3.1(f)/Schedule 3.7: Schedules control over general base statements. Schedule 3.7's two pending regulatory inquiries must be disclosed, but must NOT operate as MAE or indemnity safe harbors — see restored MAE definition and Article VII.}

Section 3.2 Bank Representations. The Bank represents and warrants that:
(a) it is a [bank / regulated depository institution] duly organized and validly existing under the laws of its jurisdiction;
(b) it has the power and authority to enter into and perform this Agreement;
(c) this Agreement has been duly authorized, executed, and delivered;
(d) the individual executing this Agreement on behalf of the Bank is authorized to do so; and
(e) [INSERT: each Deposit Account is maintained in the ordinary course of the Bank's deposit-taking business and is identified on the Bank's books in the name of the Grantor as set forth on the Account Details Schedule.]

───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ARTICLE IV — COVENANTS; BANK DUTIES; SECOND PRIORITY MATTERS
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Section 4.1 Grantor Covenants. The Grantor covenants that it shall:
(a) maintain each Deposit Account in full force and free of undisclosed Liens;
(b) [INSERT: direct all proceeds of Collateral and other collections required by the Credit Agreement cash-management provisions into Deposit Accounts subject to this Agreement;]
(c) not permit any Person other than the Secured Party to have "control" (UCC §9-104) over any Deposit Account;
(d) execute and deliver such further documents and take such further actions as the Secured Party or the Bank may reasonably request to perfect, maintain, or enforce control; and
(e) [INSERT: promptly (and in any event within three (3) Business Days) notify the Secured Party of any regulatory inquiry, action, freeze, garnishment, levy, or legal process affecting any Deposit Account, including any development in the matters disclosed on Schedule 3.7.]

Section 4.2 Bank Duties and Standard of Care.
(a) The Bank undertakes to perform only such duties as are expressly set forth herein [INSERT: and in mandatory provisions of the UCC], and no implied duties shall be read into this Agreement against the Bank.
(b) The Bank shall exercise the same degree of care as it exercises with respect to accounts of similarly situated customers [INSERT: , but in no event less than commercially reasonable care].
(c) The Bank shall have no duty to inquire into the authority of any person purporting to act for the Secured Party if instructions are given in accordance with the notice mechanics of Article VIII [INSERT: , except that the Bank shall verify that any Control Notice appears on its face to be executed by an authorized person of the Secured Party in accordance with the authorized-signer list delivered under Section 8.3].
(d) [INSERT: Nothing in this Section 4.2 shall relieve the Bank from liability for its gross negligence, willful misconduct, bad faith, or material breach of this Agreement.]

Section 4.3 Permitted Bank Charges; Priority. Permitted Bank Charges may be paid from the Deposit Accounts [DELETE: with priority over the Secured Party] [INSERT: ; provided that (i) such charges are limited as defined in Section 2.3, (ii) the Bank provides monthly reporting of such charges to the Secured Party upon request, and (iii) upon delivery of a Control Notice, no charges other than Permitted Bank Charges accrued in the ordinary course shall be debited without the Secured Party's consent]. [INSERT: All other claims of the Bank are junior and subordinated to the Obligations secured by the Deposit Accounts.]

Section 4.4 Legal Process. If the Bank receives any garnishment, levy, freeze order, or other legal process regarding a Deposit Account, it shall [DELETE: use commercially reasonable efforts to notify] [INSERT: promptly notify (and in any event within one (1) Business Day after receipt)] the Secured Party and the Grantor, and shall [INSERT: , to the maximum extent permitted by law, hold the affected funds pending joint written instruction from the Secured Party and, if required by law, the process-serving authority, and shall not voluntarily turn over funds solely on the Grantor's instruction].

───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ARTICLE V — CONTROL NOTICE; REMEDIES
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Section 5.1 Delivery of Control Notice. The Secured Party may deliver a Control Notice to the Bank at any time [DELETE: following an Event of Default] [INSERT: in its sole discretion, whether or not an Event of Default has occurred (consistent with Credit Agreement cash dominion / springing dominion mechanics as applicable)]. The Bank shall have a reasonable period not to exceed [DELETE: three (3) Business Days] [INSERT: two (2) Business Days (or such shorter period as the Bank's operational standard form permits)] after actual receipt to implement exclusive control.

{Comment — §5.1: Playbook §2.3 and Credit Agreement require Secured Party discretion to activate control (springing or full dominion as applicable), not a contractual Event-of-Default precondition that impairs UCC control or cash dominion. Shorten implementation lag to Bank-form standard.}

Section 5.2 Post-Control Operation. After implementation of a Control Notice:
(a) all withdrawals and transfers shall require the Secured Party's instruction;
(b) the Bank shall wire or otherwise transfer available balances as instructed by the Secured Party to an account designated by the Secured Party;
(c) [INSERT: the Grantor shall remain liable for overdrafts and returned items, but the Secured Party shall have no liability to the Bank for the Grantor's obligations except to the extent of funds actually received by the Secured Party from the Deposit Accounts with actual knowledge they were subject to a returned-item claim, and only up to the amount so received;] and
(d) the Secured Party may rescind a Control Notice in writing, whereupon Grantor instructions may resume until a subsequent Control Notice.

Section 5.3 Remedies Cumulative. Rights and remedies herein are cumulative with those under the Credit Agreement, the other Loan Documents, and Applicable Law. [INSERT: No failure or delay by the Secured Party in exercising any right shall operate as a waiver.]

───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ARTICLE VI — [DELETE: LIMITATION OF CLAIMS] [INSERT: SURVIVAL; LIMITATION PERIODS]
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

[DELETE: Section 6.1 Limitation Period. Any claim arising out of or relating to this Agreement or the Deposit Accounts must be brought within twelve (12) months after the date the claimant knew or should have known of the facts giving rise to the claim, and in any event within eighteen (18) months after the Effective Date, or be forever barred. The representations and warranties in this Agreement shall survive only until the date that is twelve (12) months after the Effective Date.]

[INSERT: Section 6.1 Survival. The representations, warranties, covenants, indemnities, subordinations, and agreements of the parties under this Agreement shall survive the execution and delivery of this Agreement, the establishment and termination of control, any transfer of balances, and the termination of this Agreement, in accordance with the survival matrix set forth on Exhibit B (the "Survival Matrix"), which is incorporated herein. Without limiting Exhibit B:

(a) Fundamental Representations (including authority, enforceability, ownership of Deposit Accounts, no conflicting control agreements, and creation/perfection/priority acknowledgments) shall survive until the date that is six (6) years after the termination of this Agreement and the Payment in Full of the Obligations (or the applicable statute of limitations, if longer);

(b) General Representations shall survive until the date that is three (3) years after the Effective Date, or if later, three (3) years after the date the applicable Deposit Account was added;

(c) Covenants shall survive until fully performed or waived in writing by the beneficiary thereof;

(d) Indemnification obligations under Article VII shall survive indefinitely with respect to claims asserted in writing prior to the date that is ninety (90) days after the expiration of the survival period applicable to the underlying matter, and Bank indemnities for Excluded Claims and for post-control instruction compliance shall survive indefinitely; and

(e) Any survival or limitation period in the Bank's deposit account agreement or standard terms that is shorter than Exhibit B is hereby overridden as among the parties with respect to the subject matter of this Agreement.

Section 6.2 No Shortening of Credit Agreement Survival. Nothing in this Agreement shall shorten, limit, or modify any survival, claim, or indemnity period under the Credit Agreement or any other Loan Document. Exhibit B controls over any contrary limitation period in any counterparty draft of this Agreement.]

{Comment — Art. VI: WALK-AWAY ISSUE per controlling partner instruction. Counterparty's new limitation period (12 months / 18 months outside date) contradicts Exhibit B Survival Matrix and silently shortens core representation survival. ISSUES AND RISK MEMORANDUM
Account Control Agreement — Counterparty Paper Review

To:      Deal Team / Partner
From:    Contracts Counsel
Date:    [Closing timeline]
Re:      Counterparty draft Account Control Agreement — deviation analysis, risk ratings, and recommended positions
Related: aca-redline.docx (tracked-changes redline incorporating all required modifications)

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

We reviewed the counterparty's draft Account Control Agreement ("ACA") against:

  (i)   the firm's internal ACA / cash-control playbook;
  (ii)  the executed Credit Agreement (definitions, collateral, cash management, indemnity, and survival architecture);
  (iii) the depository bank's standard control-agreement form and operational constraints;
  (iv)  the Account Details Schedule and closing checklist items for perfection by control;
  (v)   Schedules 3.7 and 5.2 and Exhibit B (Survival Matrix); and
  (vi)  controlling deal-team correspondence (latest partner instruction).

The counterparty's revision accepts most firm-standard architecture but introduces three primary silent deviations, each of which intersects scheduled disclosures:

  1. Indemnification cap silently reduced; basket converted from deductible to tipping basket
     → interacts with Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities (risk of silent shift onto Secured Party).

  2. Material Adverse Effect definition expanded with regulatory-action carve-outs of the type
     at issue on this matter → intersects Schedule 3.7's two pending regulatory inquiries.

  3. New limitation period shortens survival for core representations
     → directly contradicts Exhibit B Survival Matrix.

Controlling client instruction (latest partner email — supersedes earlier contrary priority ordering in the same thread):

  • Client WILL CONCEDE the basket conversion (tipping vs. deductible) as a commercial point
    in contexts where a basket is appropriate.
  • Client treats ANY survival-period reduction as a WALK-AWAY issue.

Misfiled administrative correspondence from an unrelated engagement was present in the matter folder and was NOT relied upon.

A full tracked-changes redline implementing the positions below is set out in aca-redline.docx.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
II. CONTROLLING INSTRUCTIONS AND SOURCE HIERARCHY
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Source hierarchy applied in this review:

  1. Controlling partner email (latest message): concede basket conversion; survival reduction = walk-away.
  2. Exhibit B Survival Matrix and Schedules 3.7 / 5.2 (scheduled exceptions control over general base text).
  3. Executed Credit Agreement (MAE, cash dominion/control, uncapped borrower indemnity customs for ACAs, collateral covenants).
  4. Internal ACA Playbook (control mechanics, bank subordination, termination, notice effectiveness).
  5. Depository bank standard form (operational SLAs for control-notice implementation, fee carve-outs).
  6. Counterparty draft (accepted only where consistent with 1–5).

Distractor materials (unrelated engagement correspondence) ignored in full.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
III. DETAILED ISSUE ANALYSIS
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ISSUE 1 — Indemnification Cap Reduction and Basket Conversion
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Section references (counterparty draft): §7.1(b) (and related tipping-basket mechanics).
Redline response: Article VII — delete cap and basket; insert uncapped Grantor indemnity; add §7.3 anti-shift for Schedule 5.2.

Playbook / precedent requirement:
  ACA Playbook §5.1 and market standard for three-party control agreements require the Grantor to provide an uncapped indemnity to the Bank and Secured Party for claims arising from account operation, instructions, returned items, and maintenance of control, subject only to a gross-negligence / willful-misconduct / bad-faith carve-out for the indemnified person. Caps and baskets are off-market on ACAs (they are M&A purchase-agreement constructs). Credit Agreement borrower indemnity architecture is likewise uncapped for collateral/control documentation.

Deviation:
  Counterparty silently (a) reduced the indemnification cap to a fixed dollar amount and (b) converted the basket from a deductible (true deductible / excess-only) to a tipping basket (once exceeded, recovery from dollar one). Neither limitation appears in firm standard or Bank form for this product.

Interaction with Schedule 5.2:
  Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities. If a cap/basket applies, claims that economically relate to those retained liabilities can be stranded above the cap or inside the basket, silently shifting residual exposure to the Secured Party or Bank — contrary to the commercial deal allocation. Schedules control over general statements; the deliverable must neutralize this shift.

Risk rating: HIGH
  (Elevated to HIGH because of Schedule 5.2 interaction; pure basket-type debate would otherwise be MEDIUM/LOW per client concession authority.)

Exposure analysis:
  • Perfection and enforcement risk secondary; primary risk is post-default / post-control monetary exposure and Bank friction.
  • Bank may refuse to sign or may demand Secured Party backstop if Grantor indemnity is capped — creates closing risk and potential Secured Party deepening-control liability.
  • Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities could migrate into uninsured/unindemnified zone.
  • Tipping vs. deductible economics matter only if a basket exists; on an uncapped ACA indemnity the point is moot.

Recommended position:
  1. REJECT any indemnification cap on Grantor indemnity under the ACA — walk-back to uncapped.
  2. DELETE basket entirely from ACA (whether deductible or tipping).
  3. NOTE for negotiation posture: consistent with controlling instruction, if counterparty insists on a basket concept in some other document, client can concede tipping vs. deductible there; do NOT import that concession into the ACA.
  4. INSERT express Schedule 5.2 anti-shift clause (§7.3 of redline).
  5. PRESERVE Bank liability for Excluded Claims and failure to honor Control Notices without cap (§7.4).

Fallback (only if Bank form absolutely requires a fee-related limitation):
  Limit any "cap" discussion to Permitted Bank Charges mechanics under §2.3 / §4.3 — not to Grantor indemnity for third-party claims or control failures.

───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ISSUE 2 — Material Adverse Effect Regulatory Carve-Outs
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Section references (counterparty draft): §1.1 definition of "Material Adverse Effect."
Redline response: Delete counterparty MAE; insert Credit Agreement-aligned MAE with express anti-carve-out for regulatory matters affecting accounts/collateral/control; conform §3.1(f).

Playbook / precedent requirement:
  Playbook §4.2 and Credit Agreement §1.01 MAE definition do not permit a broad carve-out for "any regulatory action, inquiry, investigation, examination, or proceeding." Lender-protective MAE must preserve the Secured Party's ability to treat material regulatory events affecting collateral, enforceability, or control as MAE events. Disclosures on schedules qualify representations; they do not rewrite MAE.

Deviation:
  Counterparty added carve-outs for regulatory action "of exactly the kind at issue in this matter," plus changes in law/policy and scheduled matters. This is a silent, high-impact rewrite.

Interaction with Schedule 3.7:
  Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries that intersect the very carve-outs counterparty proposes. If accepted, the draft would convert a disclosed risk into a contractual safe harbor, preventing MAE (and potentially related covenant/default) consequences even if those inquiries mature into material impairment of the Deposit Accounts or Liens. Scheduled exceptions control disclosure of facts; they must not be laundered into MAE exclusions.

Risk rating: HIGH

Exposure analysis:
  • Could nullify MAE-based leverage if Schedule 3.7 inquiries escalate (freeze, receivership restriction, enforcement order affecting accounts).
  • Impairs alignment with Credit Agreement MAE — document conflict risk and amendment/waiver complexity.
  • Undermines §4.1(e) prompt-notice covenant economics if the same regulatory events are definitionally "carved out" of materiality.
  • Off-market relative to sponsor/credit-fund ACA practice on controlled cash.

Recommended position:
  1. REJECT counterparty MAE carve-outs in full.
  2. RESTORE Credit Agreement-aligned MAE (business/condition; payment and material performance ability; validity/enforceability/perfection/priority; Secured Party rights/remedies).
  3. EXPRESSLY state that Schedule 3.7 disclosures do not qualify or carve out MAE, indemnity, covenants, or remedies.
  4. REQUIRE Grantor prompt notice of developments in Schedule 3.7 matters (§4.1(e)).
  5. KEEP Schedule 3.7 as a representation disclosure only (§3.1(f) proviso).

Fallback:
  If counterparty demands some regulatory carve-out for ordinary-course supervisory exams, limit it to routine, non-enforcement safety-and-soundness examinations that do not target the Deposit Accounts, Collateral, Loan Documents, or Secured Party Liens — and expressly exclude the Schedule 3.7 matters and any enforcement, freeze, or receivership process.

───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ISSUE 3 — Survival / Limitation Period Shortening (WALK-AWAY)
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Section references (counterparty draft): Article VI / §6.1 (12-month know-or-should-have-known; 18-month outside date; 12-month rep survival).
Redline response: Delete counterparty §6.1 in full; insert Exhibit B-aligned survival article; add Credit Agreement non-shortening protection.

Playbook / precedent requirement:
  Exhibit B Survival Matrix is the controlling survival architecture for this documentation set. Fundamental representations (authority, enforceability, account ownership, no competing control agreements, UCC control acknowledgment) survive six years after ACA termination and Payment in Full (or longer statute of limitations). General reps: three years. Indemnities: assertion window tied to underlying survival; indefinite for specified Bank failures and Schedule 5.2-related claims. Credit Agreement claim periods must not be shortened by the ACA.

Deviation:
  Counterparty inserted a new limitation period requiring claims within 12 months after discovery and in any event within 18 months after the Effective Date, and cut representation survival to 12 months after the Effective Date. This contradicts Exhibit B and is off-market for fundamental collateral/control reps.

Controlling client instruction:
  ANY survival-period reduction is a WALK-AWAY issue. Earlier messages in the partner thread stating the opposite priority ordering are superseded; only the latest message controls.

Risk rating: CRITICAL (WALK-AWAY)

Exposure analysis:
  • Fundamental control and ownership reps could expire while the facility remains outstanding — catastrophic for perfection challenges, competing control agreements, or Bank repudiation discovered later.
  • Indemnity claims for slow-developing account issues (fraudulent instructions, misdirected wires, regulatory freezes tied to Schedule 3.7) could be time-barred before discovery.
  • Direct conflict with Exhibit B creates internal inconsistency and enforceability disputes.
  • Potential adverse effect on assignability / secondary-market appetite for the credit if control docs have substandard survival.

Recommended position:
  1. WALK-AWAY from any shortening of Exhibit B periods — non-negotiable per client.
  2. DELETE counterparty limitation period in full.
  3. INCORPORATE Exhibit B by reference; attach as exhibit to ACA.
  4. OVERRIDE shorter periods in Bank deposit-account standard terms as among the parties for ACA subject matter.
  5. STATE expressly that Credit Agreement survival/claim periods are unaffected.

Fallback:
  None on fundamental reps or indemnity assertion structure. Cosmetically, a knowledge-qualified notice procedure for general (non-fundamental) reps may be discussed only if it does not reduce Exhibit B end dates.

───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ISSUE 4 — Control Mechanics and UCC §9-104 Acknowledgment
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Section references: §2.2, §5.1, §8.2; closing checklist Item C-4.
Redline response: Insert express control acknowledgment; remove Event-of-Default precondition to Control Notice; shorten implementation lag; make Control Notice effective on actual receipt.

Playbook / precedent requirement:
  Playbook §§2.1–2.3 require (a) express acknowledgment that the ACA confers control under UCC §9-104(a)(2), (b) Secured Party right to deliver Control Notice in its discretion (aligned with Credit Agreement cash dominion — springing or full), not solely post-Event of Default, and (c) effectiveness on actual receipt, not Bank acknowledgment (acknowledgment can be gamed or delayed).

Deviation / gap:
  Counterparty draft used generic "instructions" language without clear entitlement-order / control acknowledgment; conditioned Control Notice on Event of Default; allowed up to three Business Days to implement; and tied effectiveness to Bank acknowledgment.

Risk rating: HIGH (perfection / cash dominion)

Exposure analysis:
  • Missing §9-104 acknowledgment creates audit and enforcement friction; checklist Item C-4 flags as closing condition.
  • EOD gate on Control Notice can break springing cash dominion and delay lock-down when acceleration is contested.
  • Acknowledgment-based effectiveness is a classic Bank-friendly delay tactic.

Recommended position:
  Accept Bank's operational need for a short implementation window (redline: two Business Days or Bank-form standard if shorter), but REJECT EOD precondition and acknowledgment-as-effectiveness. INSERT express UCC control recital.

───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ISSUE 5 — Bank Lien Subordination and Setoff Waiver
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Section references: §2.3, §4.3.
Redline response: Broad subordination to Secured Party Lien; narrow Permitted Bank Charges carve-out; express waiver of affiliate/setoff exposure; continuing until Payment in Full + release.

Playbook / precedent requirement:
  Playbook §3.1 and Credit Agreement cash-management / negative-pledge architecture require Bank to subordinate all liens/setoff rights other than ordinary-course account fees, returned items, and corrections. Affiliate cross-setoff must be waived.

Deviation / gap:
  Counterparty/bank-leaning text limited subordination "to the extent of collected balances available after payment of the Bank's fees" and omitted broad affiliate setoff waiver — effectively preserving Bank priority and cross-product setoff.

Risk rating: HIGH

Exposure analysis:
  • On default, Bank could drain controlled accounts via setoff against unrelated credit exposure, defeating cash collateral.
  • Conflicts with Credit Agreement first-priority collateral package.

Recommended position:
  Restore full subordination + setoff waiver with narrow Permitted Bank Charges only; continuing and irrevocable until formal release.

───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ISSUE 6 — Account Information, Additional Accounts, and Exclusive Control Covenant
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Section references: §§2.1, 2.4, 2.5, 2.6, 4.1.
Redline response: Mandatory addition of new accounts; concurrent statements to Secured Party; no competing control agreements; Grantor covenant to route Credit Agreement-required proceeds into controlled accounts.

Playbook / precedent requirement:
  All Grantor deposit accounts at the Bank should be covered or become covered; Secured Party needs ongoing visibility; exclusive control covenant is standard.

Risk rating: MEDIUM

Recommended position:
  Adopt redline enhancements; require short-form joinder for new accounts on request.

───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ISSUE 7 — Legal Process / Garnishment Notice
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Section references: §4.4.
Redline response: Replace "commercially reasonable efforts" with prompt notice (≤1 Business Day) and hold-funds protocol to maximum extent permitted by law.

Risk rating: MEDIUM

Exposure analysis:
  Delayed notice of levy/freeze impairs Secured Party's ability to intervene and may interact with Schedule 3.7 regulatory scenarios.

Recommended position:
  Hard prompt-notice standard; no voluntary turnover on Grantor-only instruction when process is pending.

───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ISSUE 8 — Bank Termination Rights
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Section references: §9.2.
Redline response: Extend notice from 30 to 90 days; condition effectiveness on successor control agreement acceptable to Secured Party; migration cooperation.

Playbook / precedent requirement:
  Playbook §6.2 — Bank cannot unilaterally exit on short notice in a manner that strands perfection by control.

Risk rating: MEDIUM-HIGH

Recommended position:
  Successor-control condition is required; 90-day notice minimum.

───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ISSUE 9 — Notice Effectiveness, Governing Law, Order of Precedence, Credit Agreement Protection
